accepted.s: From which year did the Communist Party of India demand the formation of Visalandhra?
accepted.x: The Communist Party of India demanded Visalandhra from 1946 and subsequently popularised the demand through various forms of publicity.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the earliest year associated with the movement.
accepted.sec: Communist Party role - leaders, slogans, election use

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT used by the Communist Party to propagate the demand for Visalandhra?
accepted.x: The Communist Party propagated Visalandhra through songs, poems, books, pamphlets and its press. Constitutional amendments in Parliament were not mentioned as a method of its campaign.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated set of propaganda methods.
accepted.sec: Communist Party role - leaders, slogans, election use

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Puchalapalli Sundarayya — Communist leader associated with the Visalandhra campaign
Ravi Narayana Reddy — Founder of the Visalandhra Mahasabha
Baddam Ella Reddy — Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission
Arutla Ramachandra Reddy — Editor of the first issue of Visalandhra
accepted.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was one of the principal Communist leaders associated with the Visalandhra campaign. The other persons were also associated with the Communist movement, but the roles assigned to them are not supported here.
accepted.tq: Use the person–role association and reject swapped political roles.
accepted.sec: Communist Party role - leaders, slogans, election use

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Communist Party and the Visalandhra movement:
1. The Hyderabad State Communist Party practically functioned as a branch of the Andhra Communist Party headquartered at Vijayawada.
2. Communists became a major political force in Telangana.
3. The Communist Party opposed integrated linguistic states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Communists propagated Visalandhra and supported the integration of Telugu-speaking areas.
accepted.tq: Identify the single reversed political position among otherwise related statements.
accepted.sec: Communist Party role - leaders, slogans, election use

accepted.s: Why did the Communist Party intensify its campaign for a united state after the 1952 elections?
o: It had lost all representation in Telangana and Andhra.
The Hyderabad State Congress had formally joined the Communist Party.
It had made major gains in both Telangana and Andhra and expected a united state to give it a majority.
The States Reorganisation Commission had already recommended Visalandhra.
accepted.x: The Communists made substantial gains in both Telangana and Andhra in the 1952 elections and believed that a united state would provide them a majority.
accepted.tq: Link the electoral result with the political strategy that followed.
accepted.sec: Communist Party role - leaders, slogans, election use

accepted.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded on 26 November of which year at Vijayawada?
accepted.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded at Vijayawada on 26 November 1949.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the organisation’s founding year from the years of its later sessions.
accepted.sec: Visalandhra Mahasabha - founding year, venue, president, secretary

accepted.s: Who was the founder-leader of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
accepted.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the founder-leader of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
accepted.tq: Use direct founder–organisation recall rather than confusing the later presidents or campaign leaders.
accepted.sec: Visalandhra Mahasabha - founding year, venue, president, secretary

accepted.s: Who presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
accepted.x: Hayagreevachari presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
accepted.tq: Separate the session president from the founder and the president of the later session.
accepted.sec: Visalandhra Mahasabha - founding year, venue, president, secretary

accepted.s: Who presided over the 1954 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
accepted.x: Sri Sri was the president of the 1954 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
accepted.tq: Use the year to distinguish the 1954 session from the 1950 session.
accepted.sec: Visalandhra Mahasabha - founding year, venue, president, secretary

accepted.s: Who coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and wrote Visalandhralo Prajarajyam?
accepted.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and authored Visalandhralo Prajarajyam.
accepted.tq: Directly associate the slogan-related publication with its author and campaigner.
accepted.sec: Leaders → role

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Puchalapalli Sundarayya is correct?
1. He started the Visalandhra paper.
2. He later became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964.
3. He presided over the 1954 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Sundarayya started the Visalandhra paper and became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964. Statement 3 is incorrect; Sri Sri presided over the 1954 session.
accepted.tq: Separate a leader’s documented roles from the role of another associated person.
accepted.sec: Leaders → role

accepted.s: Which group mainly explained the benefits of Visalandhra through books, pamphlets and tours?
o: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar
Mir Mohammed Ali Khan, Makhdoom Mohiuddin and Mehdi Nawaz Jung
Harishchandra Heda, J.V. Narsing Rao and Arige Ramaswamy
Kodati Rajalingam, Hayagrivachari, Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao and Paga Pulla Reddy
accepted.x: Kodati Rajalingam, Hayagrivachari, Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao and Paga Pulla Reddy explained the benefits of Visalandhra through books, pamphlets and tours.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete group associated with a particular campaign activity.
accepted.sec: Leaders → role

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the mobilisation of Muslim support in Hyderabad?
o: Mir Mohammed Ali Khan — Deputy Mayor
Makhdoom Mohiuddin — Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission
Mehdi Nawaz Jung — General Secretary of CPI(M)
Mir Mohammed Ali Khan — President of the 1954 Visalandhra Mahasabha
accepted.x: Mir Mohammed Ali Khan was a Deputy Mayor and, along with Makhdoom Mohiuddin and Mehdi Nawaz Jung, helped educate Muslim opinion in Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Use the precise office attached to one member of the Muslim-support group.
accepted.sec: Leaders → role

accepted.s: In which month and year did the daily Visalandhra, started by the Communists on Sundarayya’s initiative, begin publication?
accepted.x: The daily Visalandhra began publication in June 1952 on the initiative of Puchalapalli Sundarayya.
accepted.tq: Combine the publication’s month with its year to distinguish it from related political events.
accepted.sec: Visalandhra newspaper → year + editor

accepted.s: Which publications were associated with the Communist campaign for the merger of Telugu-speaking areas?
accepted.x: The Communist Party organ Visalandhra and Sundarayya’s Visalandhra Prajarajyam campaigned for the merger of Telugu-speaking areas.
accepted.tq: Match the campaign with the two publications directly linked to it.
accepted.sec: Visalandhra newspaper → year + editor

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Event)
a. Nehru announced the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha
b. States Reorganisation Commission was constituted
c. Report of the Commission

d. Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded
List-II (Date/Year)
i. 1949
 ii. 22 December 1953
 iii. 29 December 1953
 iv. 1955
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Nehru announced the Commission on 22 December 1953; it was constituted on 29 December 1953; its report came in 1955; and the Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded in 1949.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure date and complete the chronological pairs.
accepted.sec: Representations to the SRC

accepted.s: Who announced the appointment of the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha on 22 December 1953?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru announced the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha on 22 December 1953.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the political authority making the announcement from the members of the Commission.
accepted.sec: Representations to the SRC

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission was constituted on 29 December 1953 through which instrument?
accepted.x: The Commission was constituted on 29 December 1953 through Home Ministry Resolution 53/69/53.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official instrument and number rather than only the date.
accepted.sec: Representations to the SRC

accepted.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission?
accepted.x: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission. Harishchandra Heda was associated with Telangana political resolutions, not with the Commission.
accepted.tq: Identify the person outside the formal membership list.
accepted.sec: Representations to the SRC

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the recommendation in paragraph 386 of the States Reorganisation Commission report regarding Telangana?
o: Telangana should merge immediately without any further condition.
Telangana should permanently remain part of Hyderabad State.
Telangana should merge only after a simple majority vote before 1956.
Telangana should initially remain separate and merger could be reconsidered after 1961 with a two-thirds vote.
accepted.x: Paragraph 386 recommended that Telangana remain a separate state initially, with reconsideration of merger after 1961 subject to a two-thirds vote.
accepted.tq: Read the recommendation as a sequence of condition, time and voting requirement.
accepted.sec: Representations to the SRC

accepted.s: Which of the following territorial changes was recommended in relation to Hyderabad State by the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: Raichur and Gulbarga to Andhra, and Marathwada to Mysore
Marathwada to Andhra, and the Kannada areas to Telangana
Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore, and Marathwada to be detached
accepted.x: The Commission recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Mysore and that Marathwada be detached from Hyderabad State.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of territorial transfers without reversing the recipient regions.
accepted.sec: Representations to the SRC

accepted.s:
Which sequence correctly arranges the following events in chronological order?
A. Nehru announced the States Reorganisation Commission
B. Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded
C. The States Reorganisation Commission was constituted
D. The Commission submitted its report
accepted.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded in 1949, followed by Nehru’s announcement on 22 December 1953, constitution of the Commission on 29 December 1953 and its report in 1955.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the two December 1953 events correctly.
accepted.sec: Representations to the SRC

accepted.s: The Hyderabad Legislative Assembly debate on the States Reorganisation Commission report recorded how many votes in favour of Visalandhra?
accepted.x: Of the 147 members who voted, 103 voted in favour of Visalandhra, 29 against it and 15 remained neutral.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the votes in favour from the total membership and the other voting categories.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad Legislative Assembly debate on the SRC report

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hyderabad Legislative Assembly debate:
1. The Assembly had 174 members in total.
2. 147 members voted.
3. 29 members voted against Visalandhra.
4. 15 members were neutral.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the Assembly had 174 members, 147 voted, 103 supported Visalandhra, 29 opposed it and 15 were neutral.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical component against the complete voting record.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad Legislative Assembly debate on the SRC report

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly explains the principal employment-related apprehension of Telangana leaders before the formation of Visalandhra?
o: The States Reorganisation Commission had abolished domicile rules.
Mulki Rules protecting local employment might be weakened.
Telangana would lose all private-sector employment.
Government employment would be reserved exclusively for coastal districts.
accepted.x: Telangana leaders feared that the Mulki or domicile Rules protecting local jobs would be weakened in a larger united state.
accepted.tq: Match the regional concern with its specific institutional safeguard.
accepted.sec: Apprehensions of Telangana leaders → area

accepted.s: Which concern was associated with education and administration among Telangana leaders?
o: Educational institutions would be transferred to Mysore.
Telangana had a completely superior administrative system that would be displaced.
The more advanced educational and administrative position of Coastal Andhra might dominate public services.
The Hyderabad Assembly would lose all legislative powers immediately.
accepted.x: Telangana leaders feared that Coastal Andhra’s relatively advanced educational and administrative position would dominate public services.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise cause of apprehension rather than a general political consequence.
accepted.sec: Apprehensions of Telangana leaders → area

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the apprehension with the concerned area?
1. Revenue — Telangana’s surplus might not be spent on Telangana
2. Development — Regional economic disparities might widen
3. Employment — Mulki Rules might be weakened
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. The apprehensions concerned the use of Telangana’s revenue surplus, widening regional disparities and weakening of local employment protections.
accepted.tq: Match each area with its specific apprehension before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Apprehensions of Telangana leaders → area

accepted.s: Why did the States Reorganisation Commission recommend that Telangana initially continue as a separate state?
o: Because of apprehensions about employment, public services, revenue use and regional development disparities.
Because the Commission rejected all linguistic reorganisation of states.
Because the Hyderabad Legislative Assembly unanimously rejected Visalandhra.
Because Telangana had no Telugu-speaking population.
accepted.x: The recommendation reflected Telangana leaders’ concerns regarding Mulki Rules, domination of public services, diversion of revenue surplus and widening development disparities.
accepted.tq: Combine several related apprehensions to identify the policy conclusion.
accepted.sec: Apprehensions of Telangana leaders → area

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Hyderabad Congress resolutions:
List-I (Date)
a. June 1953
b. 1954
c. 8 July 1954
d. November 1955
List-II (Decision/Event)
i. Telangana convention backed a separate Telangana
 ii. Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
 iii. Resolution for dividing Hyderabad State into three parts
 iv. Earlier resolution was rejected and territorial representatives agreed on Maharashtra and Karnataka
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: In June 1953 the Hyderabad Congress Committee proposed three divisions; in 1954 that resolution was rejected; on 8 July 1954 the PCC delegation met the SRC; and in November 1955 Harishchandra Heda supported separate Telangana.
accepted.tq: Start with the exact 8 July date and then arrange the remaining resolutions by year.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad PCC and Hyderabad State Congress resolutions

accepted.s: What territorial arrangement did the Hyderabad Congress Committee propose in June 1953?
o: Merger of the entire Hyderabad State with Andhra State
Division of Hyderabad State into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and United Karnataka
Retention of Hyderabad State without any territorial change
Division into Telangana, Andhra State and Mysore State
accepted.x: In June 1953, the Hyderabad Congress Committee proposed dividing Hyderabad State into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and United Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Recall the three proposed successor formations without substituting later arrangements.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad PCC and Hyderabad State Congress resolutions

accepted.s: What was the position adopted in 1954 regarding the earlier Hyderabad Congress resolution?
o: The resolution was rejected, while representatives agreed that Marathwada would join Maharashtra and Kannada areas would join Karnataka.
Marathwada was assigned to Andhra and Kannada areas to Telangana.
The resolution was accepted in full and Hyderabad State remained intact.
All three proposed units were merged into a single Hyderabad State.
accepted.x: The 1953 resolution was rejected in 1954, but representatives agreed that Marathwada should join Maharashtra and the Kannada areas should join Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Distinguish rejection of the original proposal from the subsequent regional agreements.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad PCC and Hyderabad State Congress resolutions

accepted.s: Which of the following was included in the Hyderabad PCC delegation’s proposal of 8 July 1954?
o: A self-sufficient Telangana comprising nine districts, Bastar, parts of Chanda and Telugu areas of Marathwada and Karnataka
A united Andhra State including all of Maharashtra and Karnataka
A separate state consisting only of the nine coastal districts
A Telangana limited to Hyderabad city and its suburbs
accepted.x: The delegation proposed a self-sufficient Telangana of nine districts along with Bastar, parts of Chanda and Telugu areas of Marathwada and Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Check the exact territorial composition of the proposed unit.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad PCC and Hyderabad State Congress resolutions

accepted.s: The self-sufficient Telangana proposed by the Hyderabad PCC delegation was estimated to have approximately what area and revenue?
accepted.x: The proposal estimated the area at 60,000 square miles and revenue at Rs 17 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate the two figures and avoid reversing their association.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad PCC and Hyderabad State Congress resolutions

accepted.s: Why was it argued that Telangana could exist as a separate state?
o: It had no revenue surplus and therefore required immediate merger.
It had higher per capita income and revenue than Andhra State and was therefore considered economically viable.
It had already been declared a separate state by the States Reorganisation Commission.
Its population was larger than that of every other region in India.
accepted.x: The argument for separate Telangana was based on its higher per capita income and revenue compared with Andhra State, making it economically viable on its own.
accepted.tq: Connect the economic indicators with the political conclusion drawn from them.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad PCC and Hyderabad State Congress resolutions

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee resolution at Kurnool
B. Formation of the Visalandhra Mahasabha
C. Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
D. Telangana convention supported separate Telangana
accepted.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded in 1949; the APCC Kurnool resolution occurred on 30 September 1953; the Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC on 8 July 1954; and the Telangana convention took place in November 1955.
accepted.tq: Place the 1949 event first, then use the stated dates to order the later events.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad PCC and Hyderabad State Congress resolutions
